back2basics.text: The United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) is an international treaty to combat climate change by limiting global warming. The Paris Agreement under the UNFCCC sets targets to keep temperature rise below 2°C, preferably 1.5°C, and includes obligations for developed countries to provide financial support to developing countries for mitigation and adaptation.

2026-11-10-pm-1242be2caa.deck: The 31st Conference of the Parties (COP31) to the UNFCCC is being held in Antalya, Türkiye, with India reaffirming its commitment to climate multilateralism and equity. The summit faces challenges from geopolitical conflicts and financial constraints, making global cooperation on climate action complex.

mcq.stem:
Consider the following statements about COP31 held in Antalya in 2026:
1. India emphasized the principle of Common But Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities (CBDR-RC) and called for developed countries to fulfill climate finance obligations under Article 9.1 of the Paris Agreement.

body.label: India's commitment
body.text: India reaffirmed its commitment to climate multilateralism, equity, and the principle of Common But Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities (CBDR-RC), calling for a fair and ambitious outcome at COP31.

body.label: Key themes
body.text: The conference focuses on implementation, emphasizing dialogue, consensus, and action to translate commitments into progress, with special attention to just transition and adaptation needs of the Global South.

body.label: Climate finance
body.text: India stressed the importance of developed countries fulfilling their climate finance obligations under Article 9.1 of the Paris Agreement to support developing countries.

sections.heading: What is the focus of COP31 and India's stance?

body.label: Geopolitical tensions
body.text: Ongoing conflicts such as the U.S. war with Iran and Russia’s conflict in Ukraine complicate negotiations and global cooperation.

body.label: Financial constraints
body.text: There is pressure on developed countries to provide predictable climate finance, but officials warn of limited political will for new funding pledges.

body.label: Climate emergency
body.text: Extreme weather events and a strong El Nino forecast heighten urgency, with global temperatures expected to exceed 1.5°C above preindustrial levels.

sections.heading: What are the challenges facing COP31?

body.label: Electrification drive
body.text: Türkiye promotes raising the share of global energy demand met by electricity from 20% to 35% by 2035, which may cause debate over the role of fossil fuels versus clean energy.

body.label: Fossil fuel phase-out
body.text: Despite a landmark pact at COP28 to transition away from fossil fuels, COP30 ended without explicit fossil fuel mention due to opposition from oil-producing countries; voluntary roadmaps are proposed.

body.label: Adaptation finance
body.text: African countries push for tripling adaptation finance to help poorer nations manage climate impacts like sea walls and drought-resistant crops.

back2basics.text: The Blue Economy refers to the sustainable use of ocean resources for economic growth, improved livelihoods, and jobs while preserving the health of ocean ecosystems. It includes activities like fisheries, aquaculture, maritime transport, and marine biotechnology. Sustainable fisheries management ensures that fish stocks are harvested at sustainable levels, balancing economic benefits with ecological conservation.

2026-11-10-pm-2c7017fc96.deck: India is focusing on developing fisheries in Lakshadweep and Andaman & Nicobar Islands to boost sustainable marine economy and exports. This initiative is key for UPSC aspirants to understand India's Blue Economy and sustainable fisheries management.

mcq.stem:
Consider the following statements about India’s island fisheries development:
1. Lakshadweep and Andaman & Nicobar Islands together account for nearly 40% of India’s Exclusive Economic Zone.
2. The government has allocated ₹218 crore for fisheries development in Lakshadweep under PMMSY.

body.label: Marine resource base
body.text: India has a coastline of approximately 11,099 km and an Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) of nearly 24 lakh sq. km, with a marine fisheries potential of 58.6 lakh MT supporting nearly 50 lakh fishers.

body.label: Economic contribution
body.text: The fisheries sector contributes significantly to food security, nutrition, employment, income generation, and seafood exports valued at around ₹73,890 crore in FY 2025-26.

body.label: Island territories’ role
body.text: Lakshadweep and Andaman & Nicobar Islands together account for nearly 40% of India’s EEZ, providing access to rich oceanic fishing grounds and major tuna migration routes.

sections.heading: What is the significance of island fisheries in India’s Blue Economy?

body.label: Investment allocation
body.text: Under PMMSY, ₹218 crore has been allocated for Andaman & Nicobar Islands and ₹175 crore for Lakshadweep to strengthen fisheries development.

body.label: Strategic focus
body.text: The Union Budget 2025-26 emphasized sustainable harnessing of fisheries resources from the EEZ and High Seas, focusing on these island groups.

body.label: Infrastructure modernization
body.text: Investments are directed towards fish landing centres, ice plants, cold-chain networks, onboard preservation, fish aggregating devices, boat-building yards, and value-addition units.

sections.heading: How is the government promoting fisheries development in these islands?

body.label: Tuna fisheries
body.text: The government aims to double tuna production in Lakshadweep to 50,000 tonnes in five years using modern vessels and sustainable fishing methods; Andaman & Nicobar Islands have a dedicated Tuna Cluster to modernize fleets and expand cold storage.

body.label: Seaweed cultivation
body.text: Lakshadweep is notified as a dedicated Seaweed Cluster to develop large-scale cultivation, seed banks, hatcheries, and capacity building for applications in food, nutraceuticals, cosmetics, pharmaceuticals, and bio-industrial products.

body.label: Ornamental fisheries
body.text: Lakshadweep hosts over 300 reef-associated ornamental species; the plan includes establishing rearing units, promoting conservation-based collection, and improving market access for sustainable aquarium species.

sections.heading: What are the key fisheries and economic activities targeted in the islands?

body.label: Sustainability and value creation
body.text: The strategy balances production growth with ecological safeguards, aiming to move beyond resource extraction towards value addition within island economies.

body.label: Livelihood and community benefits
body.text: The focus is on enabling fishers, local enterprises, and island communities to participate meaningfully in domestic and export value chains.

body.label: Strategic maritime presence
body.text: These islands extend India’s presence across the Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal, important for accessing underutilized marine resources and enhancing maritime security.

back2basics.text: The Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, is the primary legislation that protects wild animals, birds, and plants in India. It prohibits hunting and trade of endangered species listed under its schedules. The Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES) is an international agreement regulating trade in endangered species to ensure their survival.

2026-11-10-pm-40361fd3d1.deck: The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) intercepted an illegal wildlife trafficking attempt near Guwahati, Assam, recovering two elephant tusks weighing 3.7 kg. This incident highlights the enforcement of wildlife protection laws and the ongoing challenges in curbing illegal trade in endangered species.

body.label: DRI operation details
body.text: On 5th November 2026 near Sonapur Toll Gate, about 27 km from Guwahati, DRI officers acting on intelligence intercepted five suspects on two two-wheelers carrying a bag suspected to contain elephant tusks.

body.label: Suspects' response
body.text: When intercepted, the suspects tried to flee while brandishing a Khukri and a Dao, but abandoned the bag and escaped into a nearby village.

body.label: Recovery and seizure
body.text: The abandoned bag contained two elephant tusks measuring 29 inches and 30 inches in length, weighing approximately 3.7 kg, which were seized under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.

sections.heading: What happened during the wildlife trafficking interception?

body.label: Legal protection of elephant tusks
body.text: Elephant tusks are protected under Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, and Appendix I of CITES, prohibiting trade and commercial dealings in such articles.

body.label: Role of DRI
body.text: DRI uses intelligence-led enforcement and coordination with other agencies to combat wildlife trafficking and illegal trade in protected species.

body.label: Conservation significance
body.text: Preventing trafficking of elephant tusks helps protect endangered species and supports biodiversity conservation efforts.

back2basics.text: Diplomacy involves managing international relations through dialogue and negotiation to resolve conflicts peacefully. Conflict resolution seeks to end disputes by addressing underlying issues and reaching agreements acceptable to all parties. Multilateral talks often include mediators to facilitate communication and build consensus.
